statement: The OS deny list cannot be enforced on Codex, Cursor or OpenCode; it is stated to the model instead.
rationale: Found by external audit and confirmed by measurement. Only the Ollama runner ever read denyPatterns, and a comment in opencode.ts claimed the profile enforced it, which was false. Claude applies the list through a PreToolUse hook; the other three run with their own guardrails disabled - Codex with --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox, Cursor with --force - and OpenCode does not consult its own permission.bash config in non-interactive run mode at all, tested with and without --auto. So failing over from Claude silently removed the only hard boundary in the system. The boundary is now stated in the prompt for all three, which is a soft control and labelled as one. It demonstrably works on a capable model: asked to write to HKLM, OpenCode's free model made zero tool calls, refused while quoting the rule back, and the registry was verified unchanged. It depends on model compliance, so anything genuinely dangerous must not rely on it alone. The permission.bash rules are still emitted for OpenCode in case a future version honours them.

statement: The mission executor runs a real multi-step build to completion on the free tier at zero cost.
rationale: Validated 2026-08-04 rather than assumed. A mission owned by a tier-2 worker planned itself into eight steps, wrote a working Node health-check script, executed it, corrected its own README when a count changed between runs, and committed twice. Nine sessions, every one on the opencode brain, total cost 0.0000 USD. Notably step one was 'Load Postgres connection details from skill' - the planner read the skills index and chose to use a procedure a different agent had written earlier the same night, which is the self-improving loop paying off without being prompted. One correction was needed and it was mine: max_sessions was set to 6 for an 8-step plan, so budget enforcement blocked the mission at step 6. That is the circuit breaker working correctly, not a defect. Raising the ceiling and resuming carried it to completion.

statement: Do not run OmniRoute as a gateway; speak its OpenAI-compatible protocol directly instead.
rationale: OmniRoute aggregates ~278 providers and advertises ~1.53B free tokens/month, but every free tier is a per-provider API key the user signs up for - .env.example is a list of DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, NVIDIA_API_KEY, OPENCODE_API_KEY and similar. It supplies no credentials of its own, so with none configured it routes to nothing. It is also a full Next.js app with a SQLite store, JWT dashboard auth and an Electron build, meaning a second always-on server. Decisively, the one provider in its catalog reachable without a key is OpenCode Zen, which Simba already calls directly and measured 5/5. Standing it up today would return what Simba already has, at the cost of another service. Simba instead speaks OpenAI /chat/completions natively (src/hydration/openai-compat.ts), inert unless SIMBA_OPENAI_BASE is set - so adopting OmniRoute later, or any local server, is one environment variable rather than a rewrite.
